Week 06 22 — 28 JUN

06

São João in Porto

Scroll
A noite

Porto lets a thousand
lanterns go.

The whole north of Portugal waits all year for one night. On the 23rd of June the sky over the Douro fills with sky lanterns, the streets smell of grilled sardines, and at midnight the city stays up until the river goes quiet. São João — the maddest, warmest, loudest party of the year.

The rules are simple and gloriously silly. You carry a little pot of basil (manjerico), you bonk every stranger you meet on the head with a squeaky plastic hammer, and nobody minds. By the early hours the bridges over the river are packed shoulder to shoulder, everyone watching the same lanterns climb.

We weren't going to miss it. This week we trade the quiet of Amarante for the chaos of the city — and on Sunday we finally cross the Douro into Porto itself.

“No São João bailam todos,
bailam velhos e meninos…”

On São João everyone dances — the old and the young alike.
How it's done

The rules of the night

🎈

Sky lanterns

Light a paper balloon, make a wish, and let it rise over the river with a thousand others.

🔨

Martelinho

The squeaky plastic hammer. Bonk a stranger, get bonked back. It means good luck — honestly.

🐟

Sardinhas

Grilled sardines on bread, eaten standing in the street. The smell is the festival itself.

🌿

Manjerico

A pot of basil with a tiny love poem stuck in it. You don't touch the leaves — you smell your hand instead.

Sunday

Six bridges, one river

Porto and Gaia face each other across the Douro, stitched together by bridges — and the queen of them is the Ponte Dom Luís I, Eiffel's school of iron, two decks of arches with the city's metro humming across the top.

We crossed it on foot, high above the river, the old Ribeira glowing on one side and the port wine cellars on the other. Below us: Ponte da Arrábida, Ponte do Infante, Ponte Maria Pia — each one a different century of the same engineering obsession.

Best photos of the whole trip are over in the gallery.
